title: Developer Experience: SDK guides, Quickstarts & Templates, API examples, Docs Site OPS, Top Support Issues (Canonical fixes)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This document defines standards and operating procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation related to SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operations, and the canonical fixes we provide for our most common support issues. It is intended for the DevEx team, SDK owners, and engineers who maintain public examples and runtime samples.

Scope:
- Language SDKs (Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Go, Java)
- Quickstarts and repo templates for common flows (chat, completions, embeddings, reranking, streaming)
- Canonical API examples used in product docs and SDKs
- Docs site operating cadence, CI, and release procedures
- Triage and canonical fixes for top customer support issues affecting developer onboarding

Audience:
- Developer Experience engineers and technical writers
- Platform engineers who ship SDK hooks and CI integration
- Solutions engineers and customer success who use examples in demos

Standards for SDK Guides (What every SDK guide must include)
1. Short summary (1-2 sentences) describing the SDK and recommended use-cases.
2. Installation section with exact commands and supported versions. Example: `pip install redwood-inference==2.3.1` or `npm i @redwood/inference@2.3.1`.
3. Quickstart that runs in <= 30s and returns a valid example response (chat or completion).
4. Auth and config section: show how to set REDWOOD_API_KEY and region selection.
5. Examples for streaming responses, function/tool calling, and embeddings where applicable.
6. Error handling and retry guidance: include default retry/backoff recommended values.
7. Compatibility matrix table for supported features per SDK version and supported model families.
8. Tests and CI checks: a small test harness example and instructions for local verification.
9. Link to canonical API examples used by docs-site (single source of truth).

SDK Guide Template (file structure)
- README.md (Quickstart + basic example)
- examples/ (chat.py/chat.js, embeddings.py, stream_example.py)
- tests/ (smoke_test.py)
- docs/ (detailed guide, changelog links)
- ci/ (workflow that lints and runs smoke tests)

Quickstarts & Templates (recommended set)
We maintain a small, curated set of quickstarts that cover >90% of entry patterns for customers. Each quickstart is a self-contained repo or snippet that can be copied into a new project. When adding a new template, ensure a maintainer is listed and a test runs in CI.

Canonical Quickstarts matrix:
| Template | Languages | Primary use | Owner | Smoke test |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| chat-starter | Python, JS | Chat + streaming + function calling | DevEx SDK | yes |
| embeddings-basics | Python, JS, Go | Creating & searching embeddings | Search Team | yes |
| rerank-workflow | Python | Candidate scoring & reranking | Applied ML | yes |
| realtime-stream | JS | Low-latency streaming for UIs | RT team | yes |
| private-deploy-example | Docker, Terraform | On-prem private deployment template | Private Deploy | yes |

API Examples (canonical snippets and rules)
- All API examples published in docs must use the canonical snippets repository and be pinned to a release tag. Avoid inlining code that drifts from the canonical repo.
- Each example must include: inputs, expected shape of output, minimal error handling, and a short paragraph describing when to use the pattern.
- Provide both REST and SDK versions for at least the primary languages (Python, JS).
- Streaming examples must demonstrate client-side cancellation and graceful fallback to non-streaming. Include server-side note: max stream idle of 90s, server cleanup is immediate on client disconnect.

Common example categories:
- Basic completion and chat
- Streaming + partial results
- Function/tool calling with safe fallbacks
- Embeddings generation + vector search example (show how to persist vectors)
- Model variant fallbacks (how to route to cheaper model on SSE or high latency)

Docs Site Operating Procedures (ops & release)
Purpose: Keep the docs site consistent, current with SDK releases, and resilient to build failures.

1) Release cadence:
- Minor SDK releases: run smoke tests and update examples in docs if behavior changes. Doc update must be in the same PR as the SDK release when examples change.
- Major SDK releases: coordinate a docs freeze window 48 hours prior.
- Quickstarts: refreshed quarterly or when major API changes occur.

2) CI checks (required for any docs PR):
- Markdown lint (mdx/mdlint)
- Canonical snippet sync check: ensures inlined examples match snippets repo
- Smoke test runner: runs the repository quickstart examples with a mock API key and records output.
- Link checker: no 404s on internal anchors

3) Rollback & hotfixes:
- If a release causes build or customer regressions, revert the docs change and re-run CI.
- Hotfix process: create a branch docs/hotfix/<issue-id>, include test demonstrating the fix, and request an expedited review from at least one reviewer listed on the doc metadata.

Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes (current canonical list)
Below are the top recurring issues reported by support, prioritized with detection signals, temporary workarounds, and permanent fixes. Keep this section up to date - triage owners should update their canonical fix within 48 hours of a confirmed regression.

1) Problem: SDK auth errors (401) for new accounts
- Symptoms: calls return 401 immediately after onboarding; customers using environment variables but not seeing them picked up.
- Detection: spike in 401s from new accounts in onboarding region, support tag "auth-onboarding".
- Workaround: instruct user to run `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...` (Linux/Mac) or `setx REDWOOD_API_KEY ...` (Windows) and restart shells.
- Canonical fix: Update SDK to read key from prioritized sources (env > config file > OS keychain). Publish patch and update Quickstart commands. Add a small diagnostic CLI: `redwood-cli auth-check`.

2) Problem: Streaming responses hang or partial content missing
- Symptoms: client receives partial data then stops streaming; no final chunk.
- Detection: increased stream-resume errors, timeouts in client telemetry.
- Workaround: retry the request non-streaming with a smaller chunk_size or turn on the retry-after header.
- Canonical fix: improve server idle keepalive to 15s, publish SDK streaming client update to automatically attempt one resume request within 3s, and add sample retry logic to streaming examples.

3) Problem: Embedding dimensionality mismatch when migrating models
- Symptoms: vector length mismatch errors when users switch model families.
- Detection: embedding index write failures and support cases referencing model id change.
- Workaround: recommend regenerating index with new model and provide migration script.
- Canonical fix: add explicit warning to quickstarts when model family differs; include automated index-upgrade script in embeddings template.

4) Problem: Example code uses deprecated SDK calls after minor release
- Symptoms: docs build warnings, failing smoke tests flagged in CI.
- Detection: canonical snippet sync check fails or linter reports deprecated API use.
- Workaround: revert to previous docs tag and notify SDK owners.
- Canonical fix: add a pre-release linter that runs against docs snippets and fails the SDK release if snippets are out of date.

Operational ownership and escalation
- Primary owner: DevEx Docs (Aisha Patel) - responsible for doc quality, examples repo, and CI pipeline.
- Secondary owners: SDK team leads for each language (assign in quickstart metadata).
- Escalation: if a canonical fix requires infra or runtime change (e.g., keepalive tuning), escalate to Eng-Platform with the tag `eng-platform:docs-hotfix` and include the smoke test reproducer.

Maintenance checklist (quarterly)
- Run the canonical-snippet sync report and fix all diffs.
- Rotate quickstart smoke-test credentials used in CI.
- Review top 10 support tags and ensure canonical fixes are <= 60 days old.
- Run a docs-site game day: simulate a docs-site outage and validate rollback steps.

Appendix: Example commands and minimal CI snippet
- Example install and quickstart (Python):
  1. `python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate`
  2. `pip install redwood-inference==2.3.1`
  3. `export REDWOOD_API_KEY="$REDWOOD_API_KEY"`
  4. `python examples/chat_quickstart.py`

- Example GitHub Actions job (smoke test):
  name: docs-smoke-tests
  on: [pull_request]
  jobs:
    smoke:
      runs-on: ubuntu-latest
      steps:
        - uses: actions/checkout@v3
        - name: setup python
          uses: actions/setup-python@v4
          with:
            python-version: 3.10
        - name: install deps
          run: pip install -r examples/requirements.txt
        - name: run smoke tests
          env:
            REDWOOD_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.DOCS_SMOKE_KEY }}
          run: pytest examples/smoke_test.py -q

How to propose a new template or change:
1. Open a PR in the canonical-quickstarts repo.
2. Include a README with scope, owner, supported languages, and a smoke test.
3. Add the template to the quickstarts matrix and tag at least two reviewers.
4. After merge, create a docs PR that references the release tag.

Contact and ownership
